title: CartLoops
label: Featured build
summary: An e-commerce experience that explores more accessible shopping through voice input and conversational assistance.
challenge: Traditional shopping interfaces can be frustrating when users need hands-free interaction or want help finding products.
build: Developed a Django-based shopping experience with product browsing, a speech-to-text interaction, and a chatbot interface. Explored how voice and conversational UX can make digital shopping more approachable.
next: Improve automated accessibility audits, integrate more reliable product search, and document deployment.
note: Specific production deployment and accessibility certification have not been verified.

title: Zero-Trust Wireless Engine
label: Team capstone
summary: A research-driven system for observing and evaluating Zigbee/IoT wireless signals with a zero-trust security focus.
challenge: IoT and wireless sensor environments need mechanisms for recognizing unusual signal behavior and supporting trustworthy device access.
build: Working with a four-person team to design a wireless security prototype. My assigned focus is dataset organization and feature extraction, including signal variance, skewness, kurtosis and environmental context. The team switched to an external Zigbee RF fingerprint dataset while waiting for hardware.
features: Python backend and local data pipeline architecture
next: Validate features on available data, integrate modeling and dashboard behavior, and document reliable evaluation.
note: Ongoing capstone; hardware acquisition and end-to-end test results are not represented as complete.

title: NEXUSDB
label: Active build
summary: A Rust database engine built from the ground up, emphasizing custom persistent storage and systems correctness.
challenge: Understand how database systems actually store bytes, interpret SQL, maintain indexes, and recover from failure rather than relying on existing storage engines.
build: Co-designing a 12-week, two-developer implementation. My ownership covers disk pages, serialization, record storage, B+ tree indexing, and transaction durability. The other developer owns SQL parsing and developer-facing interfaces.
next: Agree on storage contracts, initialize Rust workspace, write page manager tests, and verify persistence across restart.
note: The listed database capabilities are roadmap items, not completed functionality.

title: AMR Feature Pipeline
label: Research engineering
summary: Machine-learning feature engineering for antimicrobial-resistance data and genomic analysis workflows.
challenge: Turning resistance-gene annotations into useful, validated machine-learning features requires repeatable preprocessing and careful handling of sparse labels.
build: Contributed to a BioML Lab capstone exploring MEGARes-enriched ARGProfiler outputs and downstream machine-learning features. Investigated issues such as insufficient class counts for stratified cross-validation.
next: Consolidate reproducible evaluation and expand appropriately labeled datasets before drawing strong performance claims.
note: A course/research collaboration, not a published clinical tool.

title: Stored-Grain Pest Classification
label: Academic research
summary: An image-classification study comparing convolutional neural networks and vision transformers on stored-grain insects.
challenge: Explore model suitability for classifying pest images using a small three-class dataset.
build: Conducted comparative experiments with VGG and ResNet families alongside DeiT transformer variants. Organized training, evaluation, and academic reporting with a team collaborator.
next: Improve data quality, class balance and experimental rigor before using models in practical pest monitoring.
note: Experiments were exploratory; reported results should not be interpreted as deployment-grade accuracy.

title: Django E-Commerce
label: Web development
summary: A Django learning-and-build project exploring common e-commerce backend patterns and web application development.
challenge: Apply full-stack architecture to familiar commercial workflows and develop reliable development habits.
build: Created a GitHub repository and worked through the practical setup and version-control process for a Django e-commerce application.
next: Document current working functionality, add tests, and publish reproducible setup instructions.
note: Only repository/setup work is verified; no checkout or payment system is claimed.

title: Web Systems Lab
label: Technical coursework
summary: A collection of practical applications using PHP, MySQL, Node.js, Express, MongoDB, and AngularJS.
challenge: Build and debug client–server features across multiple backend and database technologies.
build: Completed exercises around validation, authentication requests, registration/login interactions, API routes, and MongoDB persistence.
next: Refactor examples into polished, independently deployable demos with security review and tests.
note: Educational implementations; avoid deploying learning authentication code as-is.

title: C++ OOP & Algorithms
label: Academic work
summary: Foundational programming, object-oriented design, algorithm analysis, and data-structure assignments.
challenge: Translate algorithmic requirements and problem-solving principles into understandable, testable implementations.
build: Worked on class design, loops, recursion, Fibonacci algorithms, AVL trees, queues, and complexity analysis.
next: Publish carefully selected original implementations with tests and technical explanations.
